note: An invented engineering framework for the placement-suggestion eval. Not any tenant's real framework.

capabilities.name: Delivery
capabilities.description: Turning plans into shipped, working software.

expectations.2: Delivers well-defined tasks on time, asking for help when blocked.
expectations.3: Delivers features end to end with little guidance, breaking work into small steps and flagging slips early.
expectations.4: Leads delivery of multi-person projects, managing scope, sequencing and risk.
expectations.5: Shapes how several teams plan and deliver, removing systemic causes of delay.

3: Split a large migration into shippable slices and reported progress weekly.

capabilities.name: Code quality
capabilities.description: Writing and reviewing code others can trust and change.

expectations.2: Writes readable, tested code and responds well to review.
expectations.3: Writes well-structured, well-tested code and gives reviews that improve others' work.
expectations.4: Sets quality practices for a codebase and raises the bar through review and tooling.
expectations.5: Defines engineering standards adopted across the organisation.

3: Review comments explain the why and suggest a concrete alternative.

capabilities.name: Ownership
capabilities.description: Seeing work through and caring about outcomes, not just tasks.

expectations.2: Follows their own work through to completion and fixes what they break.
expectations.3: Owns outcomes for their area, following up after release and closing loose ends without being asked.
expectations.4: Takes ownership of problems that span teams and drives them to resolution.
expectations.5: Owns the long-term health of a domain and the decisions that shape it.

3: Noticed a flaky job nobody owned and fixed it.

capabilities.name: Communication
capabilities.description: Sharing information clearly in writing and in person.

expectations.2: Communicates status and questions clearly within the team.
expectations.3: Writes clear designs and updates, adjusting the message to the audience.
expectations.4: Communicates complex trade-offs to technical and non-technical leaders.
expectations.5: Shapes organisation-wide understanding of technical direction.

3: Wrote a one-page design that product and design could both follow.

capabilities.name: Collaboration
capabilities.description: Working well with others to reach shared goals.

expectations.2: Works constructively with teammates and asks for and offers help.
expectations.3: Builds strong working relationships across functions and resolves disagreements constructively.
expectations.4: Aligns several teams around shared goals and brokers agreement on contested decisions.
expectations.5: Builds partnerships across the organisation that unblock large initiatives.

3: Paired with design to settle a disagreement about an empty state.

expectations.3: Mentors newer engineers through onboarding, pairing and thoughtful review.
expectations.4: Grows other senior engineers and builds mentoring practices in the team.
expectations.5: Develops technical leaders across the organisation.

3: Ran a pairing rotation for two new starters.

capabilities.name: Operational excellence
capabilities.description: Keeping systems healthy and responding well when they are not.

expectations.2: Takes part in on-call and follows runbooks during incidents.
expectations.3: Leads incident response for their area, communicates calmly and drives follow-up actions.
expectations.4: Improves reliability across services and leads major incidents.
expectations.5: Sets the reliability strategy for the organisation.

3: Ran the incident channel and posted updates every 30 minutes.

capabilities.name: Product thinking
capabilities.description: Understanding users and the business, and building what matters.

expectations.2: Understands the purpose of the features they build.
expectations.3: Questions requirements with user and business context, and proposes simpler ways to reach the goal.
expectations.4: Shapes product direction with product partners using data and user insight.
expectations.5: Influences product strategy across several areas.

3: Suggested a smaller first release that answered the riskiest question.
